clue.text: Where middle C is often ill-greened when cooked

indicators.note: cooking turns raw ingredients into something new, so the letters of the hyphenated word are rearranged

explanation.surface: A recipe in which some vegetable has gone sickly green during cooking.
explanation.walkthrough: 'when cooked' rearranges ILLGREENED into the answer. Middle C, in written music, sits on a short extra line drawn between the treble and bass staves.
explanation.definitionFit: Middle C is commonly written on a short added line above or below the staff, which is what this musical term names.

clue.text: Split and went down, pierced by killer

indicators.note: something pierced has another thing driven into it, so one word is placed inside the other

parts.note: to go down under water is to dive, past tense dived
an orc is a killer whale

explanation.surface: Someone separated and sank after being stabbed by a murderer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pierced by' puts the killer inside; 'killer' suggests a murderer but is the whale, also called an orca.
explanation.definitionFit: A couple who have split have ended their marriage legally, which is the past participle here.

clue.text: Vulgar query as to difficulty of 14 across, the one who was 18

indicators.note: vulgar speech, the stereotype of Cockney, drops the aitch, so an H is lost from the question

parts.note: asking about difficulty is asking how hard something is

explanation.surface: A coarse question about how tough the wife at 14 found it, she who suffered the fate at 18.
explanation.walkthrough: A Cockney asks 'How 'ard?', dropping the H of HARD. Catherine Howard was Henry VIII's fifth wife, beheaded in 1542.
explanation.definitionFit: Henry VIII's fifth wife was a Catherine whose surname this is, and she lost her head.

clue.text: Ends of 2 ended

indicators.note: only the two ends of the answer to 2 down are kept, losing its middle letters

parts.note: the clue number refers to the answer at 2 down, meaning split

explanation.surface: The final parts of clue 2 have come to a close.
explanation.walkthrough: Keep the first two and last two letters of the 2 down answer: DI and ED. In the theme it is also the fate of Jane Seymour.
explanation.definitionFit: To have died is to have ended, the life having come to its close.

clue.text: With name of one's own choice less deftly planned

definitions.text: With name of one's own choice

indicators.note: a plan arranges things into order, so these letters are set out afresh

explanation.surface: Something planned with rather less skill than it might have been.
explanation.walkthrough: 'planned' rearranges LESSDEFTLY into the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who names themselves takes a title of their own choosing, not one given by others.

clue.text: I rely on a young woman from Israel

indicators.note: in a down clue one piece written on another follows it

parts.note: gal is informal for a girl
to lean on someone is to rely on them

explanation.surface: A dependent man says he leans on a girl who comes from Israel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on' means placed after, because in a down entry a piece written on another sits beneath it. Galilee is a region of northern Israel.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone from Galilee, in northern Israel, is described by this adjective.

clue.text: A soldier keeping out a rodent

indicators.note: keeping something is holding it within, so the soldier surrounds the next word

parts.note: GI is an American soldier

explanation.surface: A soldier holds out against a rodent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'keeping' means the soldier holds the next word within, all after the opening A.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a burrowing South American rodent related to the guinea pig.

clue.text: Name for good manners

indicators.note: the name sits for good within the word, held inside it rather than spelt by its outer letters

explanation.surface: A name given in honour of good manners.
explanation.walkthrough: The name is held inside mANNErs. In the theme Henry VIII had two wives of this name, Boleyn and of Cleves.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a common female first name, so it is an example of a name.

clue.text: Eastern promise — it replaces the right to sum up

parts.note: E is the abbreviation for East or Eastern

indicators.note: one thing replaces another by taking its place, so the letters for it are put where the right was

parts.note: taken as written
R is the abbreviation for right
taken as written

explanation.surface: An advert's oriental allure, swapped in to stand for what is right, to summarise.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Eastern promise' is a familiar advertising slogan, but must be split; 'replaces' puts IT where the R for right stood.
explanation.definitionFit: To epitomise is to typify or sum up something in a single example.

clue.text: Gas, one taken from realm of 14 across, the one who was 2

indicators.note: something taken from another is removed, so the letter for one is dropped

parts.words: realm of 14 across, the one who was 2
parts.note: Catherine of Aragon, Henry VIII's first wife whose marriage was annulled, came from the Spanish kingdom of Aragon
A means one, as in a single thing

explanation.surface: Gas from the realm of the first wife, the one who was cast off.
explanation.walkthrough: Catherine of Aragon was Henry VIII's divorced first wife; drop one A from her kingdom.
explanation.definitionFit: Argon is an inert noble gas found in small amounts in the air.

clue.text: Completely virtuous plus 'aving the wherewithal to make tricks?

parts.note: virtuous means good

indicators.note: the clue writes having without its aitch, telling the solver to drop the H the same way

parts.note: at cards you need a hand to win tricks

explanation.surface: A Cockney card player is morally upright and holds strong cards for taking tricks.
explanation.walkthrough: A good hand at cards, said without its aitch, is 'good 'and'.
explanation.definitionFit: The informal phrase as in 'good and ready' is an intensifier meaning thoroughly.

clue.text: Flop is its first attraction, if I get a bit of a bottom line

definitions.text: Flop is its first attraction, if I get a bit of a bottom line

indicators.note: its first letter means only the opening letter of the word before is taken
the letter I gets the place of the letter for line, replacing it

parts.note: allure is attraction or charm
L is the abbreviation for line

explanation.surface: A clumsy wordplay on why a flop appeals, if one gets a glimpse of a backside.
explanation.walkthrough: Semi-&lit: Flop is both the definition and the source of F. In ALLURE one L (line) becomes I, giving AILURE.
explanation.definitionFit: A flop is something that fails completely, a fiasco.

clue.text: Ran into debt, concealing bill

indicators.note: something concealing another holds it inside, so the bill goes within

parts.note: to be in the red is to be in debt
AC is an account, which is a bill

explanation.surface: Someone ran up debts while hiding the invoice.
explanation.walkthrough: 'concealing' puts the bill inside; 'in the red' is the usual idiom for being in debt.
explanation.definitionFit: To have raced is to have run at speed, the past tense of a verb of running.

clue.text: Main female character, having lost love, pursues pet name

indicators.note: a pursuer follows behind, so the shortened character comes after the pet

parts.note: a cat is a household pet

indicators.note: having lost means one letter is dropped from the word

parts.note: the heroine is the main female character of a story
O is love, the zero score in tennis

explanation.surface: A heroine, jilted, chases after a pet's name.
explanation.walkthrough: 'having lost' drops the O, and 'pursues' places the shortened heroine after the pet. Three of Henry VIII's wives had this name.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a female first name, so an example of a name.

clue.text: Note to say thank you for announcement of meal with Bengali port

parts.note: a chit is a short note
ta is British informal thanks
a gong is struck to call people to dinner

explanation.surface: A thank-you note sent after the dinner gong at a port in Bengal.
explanation.walkthrough: TA is everyday British slang for thank you.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a major seaport of Bangladesh, in the region of Bengal.

clue.text: Regular sum for all included in the end

parts.note: regular means even, as in an even pace

indicators.note: something included is taken inside, so the letter for all goes within the sum

parts.note: a tally is a running sum
U is the film certificate meaning suitable for all

explanation.surface: A regular total with everybody counted, in the end.
explanation.walkthrough: U is the British film rating 'universal', meaning suitable for all ages; 'in the end' is the definition, not part of the container instruction.
explanation.definitionFit: Eventually means finally, after a time, which is what in the end means.

clue.text: One little drink secures record likely to include name for being out of control

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one

indicators.note: to secure something is to hold it fast within, so the record goes inside

parts.note: a nip is a small measure of spirits
a disc is a gramophone record

indicators.note: to include is to take in, so the name goes inside

parts.note: liable means likely

explanation.surface: A small tot holds a record, probably naming someone as unruly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'secures' puts the record inside the drink, and 'to include' puts the name inside the word for likely, all after the I.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who cannot be disciplined is beyond control, unruly.

clue.text: Wasn't destroyed by disastrous drive versus United States

indicators.note: a disaster wrecks things, so these letters are thrown into a new order

parts.note: US is the United States

explanation.surface: A calamitous drive against America that came through intact.
explanation.walkthrough: 'disastrous' rearranges DRIVEVUS. In the theme Catherine Parr outlived Henry VIII.
explanation.definitionFit: To have survived is to have lived on and not been destroyed.

clue.text: Even if he were possibly dead, I certainly am!

definitions.text: Even if he were possibly dead, I certainly am!

parts.note: archaic 'be he' means even if he were, as in 'be he ever so humble'

indicators.note: possibly signals the letters could be arranged in another way

explanation.surface: A speaker insists that whatever his state, she is certainly dead.
explanation.walkthrough: 'possibly' rearranges DEAD into ADED. The speaker is a queen who lost her head, so the whole clue is her retort.
explanation.definitionFit: A person whose head was cut off is certainly dead, which is the speaker's boast.

clue.text: Taken from a passage, removed from the rest, about Roundhead

indicators.note: about means round, so the outer word goes around the letter

parts.note: something excepted is left out from the rest
the head, or first letter, of Round is R

explanation.surface: A Cromwellian soldier set apart from others, lifted from a passage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Roundhead' looks like a Parliamentarian of the Civil War but gives the head of Round, R, inside EXCEPTED.
explanation.definitionFit: Words excerpted have been extracted from a longer text.

clue.text: Next to "astute" in the index, home of the 8 who was 2

indicators.note: next to in an alphabetical list means the following entry, so the last letter moves on one
an index is alphabetical, so the final letter is changed to the one after it

parts.note: astute means clever

explanation.surface: A neighbouring entry to a word for shrewd in an index, home of a divorced queen.
explanation.walkthrough: After CLEVER in an index might come CLEVES, R advanced to S. Anne of Cleves, from a German duchy, was Henry VIII's fourth wife, divorced.
explanation.definitionFit: Anne of Cleves came from this German duchy, and her marriage to Henry was annulled.

clue.text: Bachelor building portable coffer

parts.note: BA is a Bachelor of Arts
a hut is a simple building

explanation.surface: A single man's shed has a chest he can carry.
explanation.walkthrough: BA here is the degree, Bachelor of Arts.
explanation.definitionFit: A bahut is an old chest or trunk, often carried when travelling.

clue.text: 8, the one that was 18, was good about field

indicators.note: about here means around, so the good word goes round the field

parts.note: bon is French for good
a ley is a field under grass

explanation.surface: A beheaded queen was good around the field.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' puts the field inside the French word for good. Anne Boleyn, Henry VIII's second wife, was beheaded in 1536.
explanation.definitionFit: Henry VIII's second wife, an Anne, bore this surname and was executed.

clue.text: Looking for former Eastern city outside the East?

indicators.note: the city sits outside, around the letter for East

parts.note: Peking is the former Western name of Beijing
E is the abbreviation for East

explanation.surface: Searching for an old Chinese capital beyond the Orient.
explanation.walkthrough: E goes inside PEKING.
explanation.definitionFit: Peeking is glancing or looking furtively.

clue.text: Little fish 14 across, the one that 17

definitions.meaning: the Catherine who outlived Henry VIII, his sixth wife

explanation.walkthrough: Catherine Parr was Henry VIII's last wife, who outlived him.
explanation.definitionFit: A young salmon is so named, and Henry's sixth wife bore this surname.

clue.text: Report of Hebrew climber who was European queen

indicators.note: a report is something heard, so the words are spoken

parts.note: a Hebrew is a Jew, and a liana is a climbing plant

explanation.surface: An account of a Jewish mountaineer who was a queen of Europe.
explanation.walkthrough: Queen Juliana reigned in the Netherlands from 1948 to 1980.
explanation.definitionFit: Juliana was the queen of the Netherlands, a European monarch.

clue.text: The odd one out to seem or be heard to have 4

definitions.text: The odd one out to seem or be heard to have 4

parts.words: The odd one out to seem or be heard to have 4
parts.note: among the wives she alone has a name not shared, and 'seem or' heard aloud is her surname Seymour; she died after childbirth

explanation.walkthrough: Of Henry VIII's wives, three were Catherine and two Anne; she alone stands out. 'seem or', said aloud, gives her surname Seymour.
explanation.definitionFit: Henry VIII's third wife, the only one with her first name, died soon after giving birth.

clue.text: Old magistrate about the day before

parts.note: re means about, concerning
an eve is the day before a festival

explanation.surface: An old local official around the night before.
explanation.walkthrough: RE is the Latin-derived 'concerning'.
explanation.definitionFit: A reeve was a medieval official, chief magistrate of a town or district.

clue.text: Gilbertian ship with grandmother and mother goddess cut short by student

parts.note: nan is an informal word for grandmother

indicators.note: cut short means the last letter is removed

parts.note: Cybele is the Phrygian mother goddess
L is a learner, as on a learner driver's plate

explanation.surface: A ship in a Gilbert ballad carries a granny and an abridged goddess with a learner.
explanation.walkthrough: CYBELE loses its last letter. L is the British learner-driver plate.
explanation.definitionFit: The ship in W. S. Gilbert's Bab Ballad 'The Yarn of the Nancy Bell' bears this name.
